MEASURED 2026-08-13, by running the gate on both sides of the same commit.

WHAT HAPPENED: a branch was based on another unmerged branch that had already exported. `reflow2_check` was reasoned to be safe because the chain was sound commit to commit — main `029fd47f` → `6e7f7717` → `bfcc8350`, each export recording its predecessor's content hash. CI FAILED the LINEAGE clause anyway, reporting that it found `6e7f7717` where `029fd47f` was expected.

⭐ THE MEASUREMENT, taken afterwards on the exact commit CI rejected:

    git checkout <the stacked commit>
    python3 tools/reflow2_check.py --export docs/design/reflow2.json
    → reflow2 check: OK — design and build agree (75 note(s))

**THE LOCAL GATE PASSES ON THE COMMIT CI FAILS, AND BOTH ARE CORRECT.** `_export_pair` compares HEAD against HEAD~1. Locally HEAD~1 is the branch's own parent — the other unmerged branch — so the chain checks out. In CI, GitHub Actions checks out the PULL REQUEST'S MERGE COMMIT, whose first parent is MAIN. Against that base the branch holds TWO exporting commits, which is two hops, which is the violation.

⇒ THE GENERAL FORM: **the local lineage check cannot detect a stacked-export violation by construction, because the thing that makes it a violation is the merge base, and locally there is no merge base.** A green local gate on a branch stacked on another unmerged branch is not weak evidence — it is no evidence, and it will read as reassurance.

This is not a defect in the gate. `dec:export-once-per-pr` is stated per PULL REQUEST, and the tool's own failure message already names this as its third cause — "THIS PR ALREADY HAS AN EARLIER EXPORTING COMMIT, and your chain is sound… FOLD the exporting commits into a single last commit instead" — added by `chg:lineage-message-names-its-decision` precisely because the earlier wording misled. The message was right and was reached only after CI had already spent the round trip.

⇒ WHAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT EARLIER, and it is one command rather than a build — **COUNT THE COMMITS, NOT THE PATHS**:

    git log --format=%h origin/main..HEAD -- docs/design/reflow2.json | wc -l

More than 1 means the PR violates the rule whatever the hashes say. Measured on this branch: **1** after the fix, **2** on the version CI rejected.

⚠️ THE OBVIOUS-LOOKING FORM OF THIS COMMAND IS BROKEN, and it was written into this node's first version before being caught: `git log --format= --name-only … | sort -u | wc -l` counts distinct PATHS, and since the path is pinned by the pathspec it prints 1 forever — including on the two-commit branch CI had already rejected. It is the same shape as `fact:a-piped-gate-reports-the-pipes-exit-code-not-the-gates`: a check whose output looks exactly like a pass no matter what is true.

📌 AND THE REASON A STACKED BRANCH LOOKED RIGHT IN THE FIRST PLACE, recorded because the next person will have the same reason: the requirement being satisfied existed only in the other branch's export, so basing on main appeared to risk a SATISFIES edge pointing at a node main does not hold. That worry was unfounded — the export is written from the LIVE GRAPH, which holds every branch's writes (`dec:multi-writer-architecture`; the store does not branch with git), so exporting from a main-based branch carries those nodes anyway. **The design record and the code that happens to be committed alongside it are separable, and treating them as one thing is what produced the stack.**
